title: Managed MySQL Backup Failure

compliance.assurance_rationale: Saved search evidence for AU-2 when alert outputs are archived.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `aws:cloudtrail` events with `eventName="*Backup*" OR errorCode="*"` into `index=aws`. Confirm UC-4.12.13 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `aws:cloudtrail` traffic without `eventName="*Backup*" OR errorCode="*"`. Confirm UC-4.12.13 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

description: UC-4.12.13 — Managed MySQL Backup Failure: queries multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP) `aws:cloudtrail` for `*Backup*` and returns actor, resource, and region context for reliability review and change validation.
value: On multi-cloud (AWS/Azure/GCP), `*Backup*` activity for 'Managed MySQL Backup Failure' is a high-signal control-plane change that should match approved change records and privileged-access monitoring. UC-4.12.13 drives high-priority reliability alerting before customer-impacting drift.

detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure Cloud provider TA with the modular input for `aws:cloudtrail`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.12.1.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=aws sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudtrail" eventName="*Backup*" OR errorCode="*"
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress awsRegion
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.12.13_managed_mysql_backup_fai_13"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudtrail` in `index=aws` to detect managed mysql backup failure. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the AWS CloudTrail console Event history for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_12_13_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade Cloud provider TA and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of managed mysql backup failure so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
